subject: SLA negotiation: availability smoothing and monthly credit window — Emerald Systems
messages:
From: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@emeraldsys.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@emeraldsys.com>, legal@emeraldsys.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: adjusted availability band & monthly credit window

Connor —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. As we finalize the commercial paperwork for Emerald Systems' pilot, procurement/legal asked me to flag two SLA items we need aligned before signing the MSA:

1) Availability baseline: your standard template lists 99.95% monthly availability. Given our mission-critical batch and latency-sensitive inference use, we need clarity on how short, repeated degradations are aggregated. We propose a smoothing/aggregation approach (rolling window) rather than treating each minute as an independent violation.

2) Monthly credits: we prefer a rolling 90-day lookback that smooths smaller month-to-month variance, and a cap of 45% of the invoice for any single month during the lookback. The idea is to avoid a single anomalous month wiping out our forecast.

Additional asks: carveouts for scheduled maintenance that is pre-scheduled with >=72 hours notice; a clear sample calculation for credits (hours impacted -> pro-rata credits) so our finance team can model exposure.

I've attached a short note with proposed language and examples (Emeraldsys-SLA-ask_v1.pdf). Can you let me know what parts of this you can accept and where Redwood needs guardrails?

Best,

Sasha Klein
Senior Procurement Manager
Emerald Systems
attachments: [Emeraldsys-SLA-ask_v1.pdf]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@emeraldsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability band & monthly credit window

Hi Sasha —

Appreciate the clear asks and the examples in your doc. Quick summary of what we can offer and where we'd like a middle-ground:

- Baseline: we are comfortable keeping the 99.95% monthly target. We agree aggregation matters; Redwood typically aggregates continuous short degradations into an "impact window" for remediation counting. We can share the exact aggregation algorithm.

- Lookback window: 90 days is a long smoothing period operationally. For production predictability we'd propose a 30-day rolling lookback as a compromise. That gives smoothing without holding remediation accounting open for multiple billing cycles.

- Cap on credits: we can accept a cap to reduce volatility. Our standard cap is 50% of the monthly invoice; we are open to lowering to 40-50% depending on defined carveouts.

- Maintenance carveout: we can extend the notice to >=72 hours for scheduled maintenance if it is non-emergency. For emergency maintenance we ask a narrower carveout (immediate safety/security patches).

Next steps: I attached a draft with redlines based on your PDF (redwood-sla-draft-connector.docx). Laura and Ben are copied for legal/ops nuance — Laura, Ben, any thoughts on tiered crediting vs. a single flat cap?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps speed closure.

Thanks,

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood-sla-draft-connector.docx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@emeraldsys.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability band & monthly credit window

Sasha —

Following up with operational and legal detail. Two pragmatic approaches we use with similar customers; pick which you prefer and we can prepare amendment language:

Option A — Tiered remediation credits (recommended)
- Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
- 99.90% - 99.94%: 10% credit of that month's invoice
- 99.50% - 99.89%: 30% credit
- <99.50%: 50% credit (cap)

Option B — Single-tier cap with smoothing
- 30-day rolling lookback to calculate weighted average availability; credits applied pro-rata to the impacted hours; monthly cap 40% of invoice.

Notes: both options include the following carveouts: scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice; customer-caused incidents (network, misconfiguration, third-party infra) are excluded; security emergency maintenance is excluded. For batched inference patterns we can add a specific exclusion window if you provide anticipated batch schedules.

We prefer Option A because it ties directly to severity and keeps month-to-month math simpler for ops and finance. If Emerald needs the forecast stability of a 90-day smoothing window, Option B is workable if the cap is 40% and we lock a maximum lookback at 60 days (compromise).

Action items: Sasha — confirm which option you prefer and whether you will accept a 60-day maximum lookback if you still want smoothing beyond 30 days. Ben, please flag any legal redlines we should pre-seed in the amendment.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success & Contracts
Redwood Inference
attachments: []

From: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@emeraldsys.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@emeraldsys.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability band & monthly credit window

Laura / Connor —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We discussed both options with finance and legal. Emerald prefers a smoothing approach but we are willing to accept Redwood's tiered alternative if you will:

Counter-proposal (compromise):
- Use Option B (smoothing) but with a 60-day rolling lookback (not 90).
- Monthly cap: 40% of that month's invoice.
- Credits calculated pro-rata based on impacted hours (example: credits = (hours_down / total_hours_in_month) * monthly_invoice). Please include the sample calc in the amendment.
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance >=72 hours notice accepted; security/emergency patches excluded.

If that is acceptable we will route the amendment to legal. I've attached a one-page counter with our requested language and the sample calculation (Emeraldsys_SLA_counter_v2.pdf). We'll also circulate a DocuSign for the amendment if you produce the redline.

DocuSign (tentative): https://docusign.com/EMR/eqw12345
Jira ticket for procurement flow: https://jira.internal.redwood.com/browse/PROC-987

Appreciate you both moving quickly on this — Emerald is ready to start the pilot once we have the signed amendment.

Best,

Sasha Klein
Senior Procurement Manager
Emerald Systems
